body.title: Body

about.athlete: Your weight, body fat and measurements over time. FitWise uses them to keep your calorie and macro targets in line with your body. Weigh in at least 4 days a week, ideally at the same time of day: with fewer weigh-ins FitWise can't suggest a weekly calorie adjustment. Body fat and measurements are optional. When your weight changes by 2 % or more, FitWise asks you here whether to recalculate your targets: accept or reject.

progression.title: Progression methods
progression.lead: How the weight and reps of an exercise are suggested as you train. A suggestion is never applied by itself: you accept or reject it.
progression.linear: Linear progression: one fixed number of reps. When every working set reaches it at the planned weight, the next session suggests the weight plus the increment.
progression.double: Double progression: a range of reps. First add reps at the same weight until every working set reaches the top of the range; then the weight goes up by the increment and the reps restart at the bottom.
progression.manual: Manual: FitWise makes no suggestions for this exercise. You change the targets yourself.
progression.increment: Increment: how much weight is added when the method suggests going up.
progression.deload: Allow deload weeks: after 3 finished sessions in a row below the target at the same weight, FitWise may suggest a lighter weight (90 % of it, rounded down to the plate step) and then starts counting again.

hint.linear: Linear: hit the fixed reps on every set and the next session suggests the weight plus the increment.
hint.double: Double: add reps until every set reaches the top of the range, then the weight goes up by the increment and the reps restart at the bottom.
hint.manual: Manual: no suggestions; you change the targets yourself.
